body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z):(A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\}\), with \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) returning its unique element or two attained unequal elements

sampling_model.design: The main identifying and certification class is a single stationary Gaussian fine-grid VAR(1), observed at times \(0,m,\ldots,nm\), with known \(m\), supplied labeled process DAG \(G\), triangular transition, and diagonal fine innovation covariance. The even-factor sign corollary is deliberately broader: it permits an arbitrary stable transition and arbitrary positive-definite Gaussian innovation covariance and needs no supplied order.
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are the \(n+1\) dependent coarse-time vectors \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no binary treatment; the causal query is the direct fine-grid transfer along the supplied process edge \(u\to v\).
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment-overlap condition. The stability margin gives \(|1-A_{vv}z|\ge\gamma>0\) on \(\mathbb T\), which is the support condition needed for the rational transfer.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \((M_0,M_1)\) by overlapping empirical lag moments and form \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\). On the odd target-corridor class, recover only the diagonal and edge coordinates on directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths, propagate the Isserlis long-run covariance through that localized Jacobian, and report simultaneous Wald disks. The global derivative-separated estimator agrees on the target and is a corollary. Outside the localized regular class, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all compatible fine-grid branches without selecting one.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gong et al. obtain positive fine-model recovery under non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, and separately note generic nonuniqueness under Gaussian data.
We present a unifying framework for parameter identifiability and estimation under both subsampling and mixed frequencies when the shocks are non-Gaussian.
The algorithm forms a Schur decomposition and computes a \(p\)-th root of the triangular factor by a recursion.
The spectral latent-factor half-trek criterion identifies direct link functions by rational operations on the spectral density.
We characterise the asymptotic distribution of causal effect and spectral contribution estimators in terms of algebraic relations dictated by the process graph.
We establish useful deviation bounds for dependent Gaussian data using a spectral measure of stability.
We prove an exponential probability tail inequality for positive semidefinite quadratic forms in a subgaussian random vector.
The results about coverage probability are stated in a nonasymptotic way and apply for small and moderate sample size.
We provide a constraint satisfaction procedure for system-timescale causal structures corresponding to a measurement-timescale structure.
Classical CAD projection algorithms preserve chordal structure when projection follows a perfect elimination ordering.
In the regular mixed-frequency VARMA case with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order, generic local identification fails.

body.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the complete compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root. For odd \(m\), the transfer is identified and smoothly recoverable when diagonal-root derivatives and divided differences are separated only on vertices and edges lying on directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths; the earlier globally separated Wald theorem is a corollary. For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction holds on the larger class of all stable Gaussian VAR(1) transitions with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, without an order or triangularity assumption. Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either use non-Gaussian shocks for positive recovery, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Gong et al.'s positive theorem assumes non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, so neither it nor the present Gaussian supplied-order result contains the other. No prior result identifies and infers a queried Gaussian transfer using only its directed target corridor while retaining exact ambiguity certificates elsewhere.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular divided-difference recursion available, but a direct transfer needs only the vertices and edges on directed paths from \(u\) to \(v\). Localizing root-derivative and divided-difference separation to that corridor avoids regularity assumptions on irrelevant branches. Diagonal fine innovations remain informative for complete-fiber certification, whereas the even-factor global sign calculation needs neither triangularity nor diagonal innovations.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit target-corridor identifying map and simultaneous Wald disks on a nonempty compact corridor-separated odd class, with the globally separated theorem retained as a corollary. It also gives an unrestricted stable-Gaussian even-sign obstruction with arbitrary positive-definite innovations, plus a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with attained witnesses and finite-sample branch-free inversion. The covariance-envelope fallback remains a validity device equal pathwise to the deterministic box, not a claimed adaptive improvement.

body.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate temporal causal recovery from subsampled data. Their positive recovery theorem uses non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions; the present positive result instead uses Gaussian innovations, a supplied order, and process-DAG restrictions, so the two positive classes are incomparable rather than related by inclusion. Their Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion motivates the obstruction, while the present proof isolates an even-factor sign pair on the strictly larger stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance and no order or triangularity requirement. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) likewise use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints, whereas the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply triangular-root algorithms and branch theory; the new step localizes recursion to directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths and then combines graph zeros, innovation covariance, transfer equality, and complete-fiber certification. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide concentration context for finite-sample moment regions. Mixed-frequency VARMA and unit-root results of Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) concern different model classes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The target-corridor result still assumes a supplied scientifically defensible order and an odd known sampling factor for positive identification; it does not infer the order. Genericity is in fine-parameter space, not observed-law image space. Exact CAD certifies termination but not polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. Gong et al.'s Temperature--Ozone example is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if external science supplies the one-way order; their fit does not establish that order, and their positive non-Gaussian theorem is not imported into this Gaussian class.
body.honest_scope: Positive identification and Wald inference concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) process-DAG models with known odd subsampling factor and diagonal fine innovation covariance. Point identification of \(h_{uv}\) and smooth recovery require noncollision and derivative separation only on the directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) corridor; coefficients and innovation variances outside that corridor may remain ambiguous, and no full-matrix uniqueness is claimed from localized conditions. The older global derivative-separated class is a nonempty sufficient subclass when \(\kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\). In contrast, the even-factor sign obstruction holds for every stable Gaussian VAR(1) with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, even without a supplied order, triangularity, or graph zeros, whenever the queried coordinate is nonzero. Outside the corridor-regular class, inference is branch-free. No claim is made about unknown sampling factors, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.
